themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Positions itself as India's First IVF company to list on the stock market, India's No. 1 IVF Clinic per a Times of India Health Survey, India's First IVF chain to introduce AI in infertility treatment, and India's First IVF company to receive the European Quality Award for highest quality standards.
- "Our Moat, Our Momentum" frames eleven compounding strengths built over 15+ years - established/trusted brand, clinical excellence, strong clinical leadership, integrated care platform, pan-India presence, global reach, multi-channel patient acquisition, scalable growth platform, SOP-driven operations, innovation-led care, and emotional counselling support - claiming it has already crossed every major industry entry barrier (regulatory compliance, high capital/infra costs, brand trust, tech/R&D dependence, ethical sensitivities, consolidation, skilled manpower).
- Claims a global patient base, having successfully treated patients from 30+ countries including Canada, UK, Middle East, Africa, Indonesia, Australia and New Zealand, positioning Gaudium as a fertility-care destination beyond India.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body: - Shareholding is Promoter & Promoter Group-dominated at 71%, with DII at 2%, FII at 3% and Public at 23%, as reported in the presentation.
